summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted after his Remodulin infusion catheter dislodged at home, causing minor bleeding. He presented to the emergency department where a temporary IV was placed and Remodulin was restarted. The tunneled catheter was successfully replaced on the right chest the following day without complications. Imaging confirmed proper catheter tip placement in the superior vena cava. His portopulmonary syndrome remained stable, and all home medications, including Remodulin, sildenafil, doxycycline, and pain regimens, were continued without change. He tolerated the procedure well, had no signs of infection or bleeding, and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions for catheter care and follow-up with his specialty teams.
